summary: Radar for 2026-11-02, GLP-1 focus only. The best early catch is an observational study presented at the AHA Scientific Sessions (Nov 2–6, 2026). In 256,492 adults with prediabetes and obesity, GLP-1 medicines were linked to 1.5 times the chance of blood sugar returning to normal and a 31% lower risk of type 2 diabetes compared with metformin. The study pooled semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide and dulaglutide. Only the AHA newsroom, Medical Xpress and a few others have covered it so far, and November is Diabetes Awareness Month. Because it is observational and a class-level result, it suits a 13:00 Short worded with "linked to", not a long-form. Two new Medscape items from today feed Lane A directly. The first is GLP-1 pen storage mistakes, which becomes a new practical long-form question just before Thanksgiving travel. The second is "GLP-1 therapies not linked to fracture risk", a reassurance Short that points to the Bones & Muscle long-form. Retatrutide's TRIUMPH sleep apnea Phase 3 data (AHI down up to 36.1 events an hour, 60.6%) is the strongest retatrutide hook for the 13:00 slot. For the 14:00 Lane A queue, the Oct 30 consumer article on GLP-1 fatigue and the Oct 9 regain systematic review keep fatigue and stopping fresh. Injection-site reactions, dehydration and birth control have recent journal hooks. Rejected: today's Forbes "where to buy tirzepatide" piece, the Page Six "$99" promotion, "research peptide" retatrutide sellers and online peptide-therapy launches. Couldn't verify: the Lilly "fakes up 180%" figure (only Cork Beo; I didn't find it in other outlets) and full ATTAIN-J numbers beyond the PubMed title and the 8.7% headline.

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines vs metformin in prediabetes: an AHA Scientific Sessions 2026 study of 256,492 adults with prediabetes and obesity (semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide and dulaglutide pooled). Linked to 1.5 times the chance of blood sugar returning to normal, 31% lower type 2 diabetes risk, 15% fewer heart attacks and 20% fewer strokes. Observational, about 3 years of follow-up
candidates.angle: "Prediabetes? What a 256,000-person study linked to GLP-1 medicines." Honest framing: health-record data, so it's 'linked to', not proof. GLP-1 medicines aren't approved for prediabetes alone, so explain who the approvals actually cover and what to ask your doctor. Say 'GLP-1 medicines' throughout (class study). Don't give individual drug results, because the study didn't analyse them separately.
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–8 days (AHA sessions run Nov 2–6; Diabetes Awareness Month and World Diabetes Day on Nov 14 extend it)
candidates.why_now: AHA press release out today (Nov 2) with an AHA video. Pickup is limited to Medical Xpress and the AHA site, and there are almost no creator videos yet. The prediabetes audience is a core fit, and November is Diabetes Awareness Month.

evidence.signal: 256,492 adults; observational EHR; 1.5x normoglycemia, -31% T2D, -41% all-cause death, -15% MI, -20% stroke, -25% HF vs metformin; causation not established

evidence.source: Google News: Medical Xpress / heart.org video
evidence.signal: Multiple outlets in the first hours, Nov 2

candidates.topic: Why am I so tired on tirzepatide? The Zepbound label lists fatigue in 5% (5 mg), 6% (10 mg) and 7% (15 mg) vs 3% on placebo, refreshed by the Oct 30 consumer piece 'GLP-1s and Fatigue: Why You Feel Tired'
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. First sentence: 'Feeling tired on tirzepatide is listed on the label, and for most people it's manageable.' Cover the label rates, then likely contributors: eating much less, protein, fluids, sleep. Leading explanations only, worded 'can'. Finish with when to call the prescriber. No dosing talk.

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 (783 began the lead-in; 335 vs 335 randomized; +14.0% regain from week 36 to 88 on placebo), refreshed by the Metabolites systematic review on regain after GLP-1/GIP medicines (Oct 9), Daily Maverick's 'what happens when the injections stop' (Nov 2) and Food Business News on food spending after stopping (Nov 2)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form (redo of L1 10-27). The first sentence answers it: on average, weight tends to come back when treatment stops, and staying on it helped people keep the loss. Then cover what the research says helps: protein, strength training, a plan made with the prescriber. Include 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own'.
keywords: what happens when you stop Mounjaro
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen; mainstream 'after the injections' stories rising now
candidates.why_now: Seen in 11 snapshots with momentum up to 87, and mainstream outlets covered it again today. The long-form was lost to a narration error and has high demand. Company coverage cuts in today's news (NewsNation, Starbucks) mean more people may face stopping. Cover that only as context, never as a cost topic.

'Life after weight-loss medication': mainstream pickup, Nov 2

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide pen storage: left out of the fridge, too hot, frozen, or travelling for Thanksgiving? Hooked on Medscape's 'Can Storage Mistakes Ruin a GLP-1 Drug?' (Nov 2)
candidates.angle: A new Lane A question: 'Tirzepatide pen left out: is it still OK?' Stick strictly to what the current Zepbound/Mounjaro labels and instructions for use say: refrigeration, room-temperature limits in days and temperature, don't freeze, protect from light. For travel, keep it in its packaging and carry it on rather than checking it. Don't cover vials bought outside pharmacies or compounded products. When unsure, tell viewers to ask a pharmacist or prescriber. Ties into the Thanksgiving travel window.
candidates.why_now: Medscape published this today, so clinicians are discussing it. Holiday travel questions are about to spike. Current search results are dominated by telehealth blogs with unreliable claims, which gives us room. No live Lane A video covers it.

evidence.signal: 'Can Storage Mistakes Ruin a GLP-1 Drug?', Nov 2, 2026
The SERP is mostly telehealth blogs (doctronic and others), some contradicting each other; weak authoritative competition

candidates.topic: Will tirzepatide weaken my bones? Medscape: 'GLP-1 Therapies Not Linked to Fracture Risk in Three Studies' (Nov 2), plus the Arch Osteoporos skeletal systematic review (Oct 23)
candidates.angle: 08:00 body-worry reassurance Short with tirzepatide in the title: 'Tirzepatide and bones: will it raise fracture risk?' The calm answer: three new studies of GLP-1 medicines found no link to fractures. Mostly observational and class-level, so say 'GLP-1 medicines'. New fact, then a line on strength training and protein, then when to see a doctor. Point the 20:00 funnel to the Bones & Muscle long-form.
candidates.why_now: Medscape covered it today. Our bones Short reached 242 views, second-best body-worry Short, and the Bones & Muscle long-form needs funnel traffic as a slow starter.

evidence.signal: Three studies: no link between GLP-1 therapy and fracture risk, Nov 2
Earlier data: GLP-1s may reduce fracture risk in obesity/T2D (Sep 2026)

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and sleep apnea: TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA Phase 3. In adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and BMI 27 or higher (without and with T2D), AHI fell by up to 36.1 events an hour (60.6%) from a baseline of 58.6. Medical News Today pickup Oct 30
candidates.angle: 13:00 retatrutide 'what's confirmed?' Short with a loop ending. Give the AHI drop in plain words (fewer breathing pauses an hour) and the population. Then the tirzepatide context: tirzepatide already has an FDA sleep apnea approval (SURMOUNT-OSA). Separate trials, not head-to-head. Include the 'not approved; online research products aren't the trial drug' line.
candidates.why_now: New Phase 3 retatrutide data, the format that peaks for us (273, 206, 122). Consumer pickup started Oct 30 with only a handful of creator videos so far.

evidence.signal: 'Experimental weight-loss drug retatrutide may help improve sleep apnea', Oct 30
Lilly Phase 3: retatrutide reduces OSA severity; AHI and hypoxic burden data

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions: what's normal (redness, itching, bruising) vs when to call. Refreshed by the Med Sci (Basel) systematic review of skin side effects with semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide (Oct 9), and the Cureus RCT meta-analysis of semaglutide skin adverse events
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. The first sentence answers it: mild redness or itching where you inject is a known, usually short-lived side effect. Use label rates. Practical, label-based tips (rotate sites as the instructions say). Signs that need a prescriber, and allergic-reaction signs that need emergency help right away. Don't tag our own tips to the label.
candidates.why_now: In the playbook's Lane A queue. Two new systematic reviews give a fresh evidence hook. The S1 injection-site Short shipped 11-02, so a long-form becomes its funnel target.

evidence.signal: Systematic review of skin adverse events with semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide, Oct 9
Meta-analysis of RCTs on skin adverse events with semaglutide

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and birth control pills: what the label says (reduced oral contraceptive exposure after starting and after each dose increase; the label advises a non-oral or backup method for 4 weeks). Refreshed by the Front Pharmacol pregnancy-outcomes meta-analysis (Oct 16) and the US claims study of anti-obesity medication exposure before and during pregnancy (Oct 15)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: report the label only, no instructions. Explain why: slower stomach emptying can affect pill absorption. Report what the meta-analysis found without overstating it. Send viewers to their prescriber or pharmacist. No 'Ozempic babies' hype.
candidates.why_now: In the playbook's Lane A queue, with two new pregnancy-exposure papers in October. Many women of reproductive age are on tirzepatide (the label figure is 7.1% vs 0.5% in women for hair loss, showing the size of the female audience). Search demand is steady and under-served.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and dehydration: signs and what helps. The label warns about acute kidney injury linked to dehydration from vomiting or diarrhea. Refreshed by the J Clin Med cohort on kidney stone recurrence after starting GLP-1-based therapy (hydration factors, Oct 16)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. The first sentence answers it: eating and drinking less, plus stomach side effects, can leave you low on fluids, and the label warns this can affect the kidneys. Practical: sipping through the day, fluids from food, warning signs, when to call the prescriber, and when to get help right away. Present the kidney-stone cohort as observational and 'linked to'.
candidates.why_now: In the playbook's Lane A queue. It pairs with fatigue (shared causes) for 'watch next' linking, and no live Lane A video covers it.

candidates.topic: Are GLP-1 medicines safe if you're frail or over 65? JAMA analysis 'Are GLP-1 Drugs Safe in People With Frailty?' (Oct 30), SELECT frailty post hoc (semaglutide 2.4 mg; 17,604 adults with heart disease and BMI 27 or higher, no diabetes; benefit consistent across frailty levels), and the age-group heart meta-analysis of RCTs (Oct 27)
candidates.angle: 08:00 reassurance plus honest-uncertainty Short. Benefit held across frailty levels in SELECT, which was a post hoc analysis. What's still unknown: muscle and nutrition in older adults. Protein and strength as the practical bridge. Semaglutide-only evidence, so a semaglutide title is allowed; stick to SELECT's population.
candidates.why_now: A new JAMA news analysis plus two recent journal papers. Medicare-age interest is high, though it's a semaglutide-only angle and those titles underperform for us.

evidence.signal: 'Analysis Asks: Are GLP-1 Drugs Safe in People With Frailty?', Oct 30
